home.name: Sebastián Paternostro
home.shortBio: I design online stores and websites and set them up on the platform. Structure, interface, and review through launch.
home.howTitle: How I take a store live
home.howSubtitle: The work is design and setup on the platform. Backend and custom integrations belong to development.
home.howOneDesc: I learn what the business sells and how people order. Then I organize categories, pages, and the path to checkout.
home.howTwoDesc: I set it up on TornadoStore, GlobalBluePoint, or TiendaNube, and I adjust HTML and CSS when needed. An ERP connection or a payment gateway is programmed by development. I specify it and review it.
home.howThreeDesc: I compare the implementation with what was supposed to ship, write down what is broken, and train the person who will run it.
home.highlight1Desc: The store moved off Mercado Shops onto its own platform before the marketplace shut down. I handled structure, interface, and follow-up with development through launch.
home.highlight2Desc: Catalog and B2B ordering for an auto-accessories wholesaler. The site replaces phone and spreadsheet orders.
home.highlight3Desc: A demonstration store, not a client project. It shows how I build an ecommerce site from scratch inside TiendaNube.
home.highlight4Desc: Full brand and web redesign for a premium mobile bar service, translating a high-end experience into a functional digital portal with dynamic media integration.
home.philosophy: A store works when someone can find the product and place the order. The rest is decoration.
home.ctaTitle: If you need someone to design the store and leave it published, this is the work.
home.location: I'm in Japan for 12 months. Looking for remote work, overlapping European and US hours. Europe after that.

At NetOne (2024–2026) I took 15+ B2B and B2C projects through requirements, structure, interface, QA, and training. principles.collaborationDesc: I gather requirements with the client and train them to operate the store without me.

gamingcity.title: GamingCity — From marketplace store to brand E‑commerce
gamingcity.intro: GamingCity needed to migrate from MercadoShops to its own platform before the service shutdown. The challenge was translating their brand identity and marketing needs into a flexible experience while working under an existing CMS.

myRole.title: My Role
myRole.p1: I owned the structure and interface of the new store, and the follow-up with development through launch. The deadline was external: Mercado Shops was shutting down.

overview.title: Overview
overview.p1: GamingCity is a hardware retailer specializing in gaming PCs and components.
overview.p2: Their previous store ran on MercadoShops, limiting brand flexibility. With the platform shutting down, they needed a system that would support growth and marketing campaigns.
overview.p3: The new site had to improve product discovery and tools like the PC builder.

beforeAfter.title: Before vs After
beforeAfter.desc: The previous store offered little flexibility. The new platform allowed GamingCity to express their brand with full clarity.

pcBuilder.title: PC Builder Experience
pcBuilder.desc: The configurator experience was refined to guide users in selecting compatible components while reducing errors.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.p1: The new platform allowed GamingCity to overcome marketplace limitations and establish a solid digital presence.
outcome.p2: The launch was completed successfully before the MercadoShops shutdown, ensuring a smooth transition.

kiro.title: KIRO — Building a Functional Ecommerce from Scratch
kiro.intro: KIRO is a demonstration store on TiendaNube. It is not a client project. I built it to show what an ecommerce site looks like when it is designed and published inside the limits of the platform.

myRole.title: My Role
myRole.p1: A solo project, with no client. I defined the structure, navigation, and presentation, and published it on TiendaNube so there is a real store to walk through.

overview.title: Overview
overview.p1: This project started with no prior structure: no existing store, no predefined navigation and no optimized product logic.
overview.p2: Unlike redesign projects, the challenge here was to build everything from zero while working within the constraints of TiendaNube's ecosystem.
overview.p3: The focus was to create a store that feels simple, clear and trustworthy for users, while remaining easy to manage from a business perspective.

context.title: Context
context.p1: TiendaNube provides a fast way to launch ecommerce websites, but it comes with strong limitations in layout flexibility, component customization and advanced UX patterns.
context.p2: This creates a common problem: stores often look generic, product presentation lacks hierarchy, navigation becomes cluttered and UX decisions are constrained by the platform.
context.p3: The challenge was to overcome these limitations without relying on custom development.

challenge.title: Challenge
challenge.item1: Build a complete ecommerce experience from scratch
challenge.item2: Avoid the 'template look' typical of TiendaNube stores
challenge.item4: Structure navigation in a scalable way
challenge.item5: Deliver a usable and realistic store without custom code

approach.title: Approach
approach.p1: Instead of fighting the platform, the approach was to design within constraints and use them strategically.
approach.item2: Use hierarchy to guide user attention
approach.item4: Leverage available components in smarter ways
approach.item5: Reduce friction in the purchase flow
approach.p3: The focus was not on 'adding features', but on making better use of what already exists.

structure.title: Product Structure
structure.desc: Products were organized to improve scanability and reduce cognitive load. Clear naming, grouping and visual hierarchy helped users quickly understand what they are looking at.

navigation.title: Navigation Simplification
navigation.desc: Menus and categories were structured to avoid unnecessary depth and confusion. The goal was to reduce decision fatigue and make browsing intuitive.

clarity.title: Visual Clarity
clarity.desc: Instead of overdesigning, the UI focuses on spacing, alignment and readability. This creates a cleaner experience without needing heavy customization.

adaptation.title: Platform Adaptation
adaptation.desc: All decisions were made considering TiendaNube's limitations. Solutions were designed to be easy to implement, maintain and scale within the platform.

visuals.title: Visuals
visuals.desc: Screenshots of the final result within TiendaNube.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.item1: A functional ecommerce that feels cleaner and more intentional than typical template-based stores
outcome.item2: Improved product discovery and navigation clarity
outcome.item3: Smoother and more predictable purchase experience

takeaways.title: Key Takeaways
takeaways.item1: Constraints don't limit design — they define it
takeaways.item2: Clarity is more valuable than customization
takeaways.item3: Structure has more impact than visuals alone
takeaways.item4: Good ecommerce UX is mostly about reducing friction
takeaways.item5: You don't need full control to build a solid product

value.title: Professional Value
value.item1: Build structured ecommerce experiences from zero
value.item2: Translate business needs into practical solutions
value.item4: Focus on usability and clarity instead of unnecessary complexity

incident.title: Incident Reporting Standardization
incident.subtitle: Cross-team process improvement through structured communication
incident.intro: Redesigned the internal issue documentation workflow to transform chaotic reporting into a highly structured protocol, reducing communication overhead and development bottlenecks.

meta.outcomeValue: Accelerated bug resolution cycles and transparent tracking

myRole.title: My Role
myRole.p1: I audited the process flaws autonomously and designed a comprehensive issue template detailing reproduction steps, exact technical contexts, and visual payloads. I drove its implementation across development teams, reducing feedback loops dramatically.

overview.title: Overview
overview.p1: The company operated under ISO-based quality procedures. However, daily execution revealed inconsistencies in how incidents were documented between Support, Design and Development teams.

context.title: Context
context.p1: Ambiguous error logging forced developers to waste extensive time mapping contexts from scratch, causing friction and long delivery delays.

situation.title: Situation
situation.p1: Incident reports often contained minimal information, forcing developers to investigate context from scratch.
situation.p2: This created repeated clarification loops, long resolution cycles and frustration across teams. Over time, frustration gradually turned into operational apathy.

insight.title: Insight
insight.p1: Operational efficiency falls apart when information handoffs are unstructured. Standardizing the mandatory documentation parameters completely solves the structural gridlock.

processChange.title: Process Change
processChange.afterItem3: Client and error contexts provided upfront

approach.title: Approach
approach.p1: Introduced an incident structure requiring clear problem categorization, current vs. expected behavior, structural screenshots, and an initial resolution hypothesis to isolate backend from frontend faults.
approach.item1: Clear problem categorization in the title
approach.item2: Explicit description of current vs expected behaviour

impact.title: Impact
impact.item1: Drastic drop in cross-department clarification requests
impact.item2: Seamless task delegation from senior to junior developers
impact.item3: Immediate status reporting availability for stakeholders
impact.item4: High volume of operational bugs resolved within 24 hours

principles.title: Key Principles
principles.principle2Desc: Strict documentation layouts prevent cross-team operational apathy.
principles.principle3Desc: Investing upfront effort into defining the issue drops engineering layout iteration loops.
principles.principle4Desc: Providing total situational data allows engineers to work without active dependencies.

biotec.title: Biotec S.A.
biotec.intro: Bilingual web design for a food technology company focused on technical clarity and international reach.

myRole.title: My Role
myRole.p1: I was responsible for the full design of the site, from structure to interface. The work focused on organizing technical information, improving content clarity, and building a solid foundation to communicate effectively in both local and international markets.

overview.title: Context
overview.p1: Biotec S.A. is an Argentine company with over 40 years in the food industry, specializing in the import, formulation, and production of additives.
overview.p2: Their offering combines technical development, quality certifications, and international supplier relationships.
overview.p3: The website needed to reflect that level of professionalism and serve as a commercial tool across different markets.

beforeAfter.title: Before vs After
beforeAfter.desc: The previous site did not represent the company's technical level or global ambitions.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.p1: The new site communicates Biotec's value proposition in a clear, technical, and professional way.
outcome.p2: It becomes a commercial tool that supports both the local market and international expansion.

accesoriosjorge.title: Accesorios Jorge
accesoriosjorge.intro: Design and development of a wholesale ecommerce focused on simplifying the purchase process and structuring commercial operations.

myRole.title: My Role
myRole.p1: I designed the full ecommerce experience, from catalog architecture to order flow. The focus was on reducing the steps required to complete a purchase and giving structure to a catalog that was previously managed manually.

overview.title: Context
overview.p1: Accesorios Jorge is a wholesale auto parts distributor with a broad catalog and primarily manual sales processes.
overview.p2: The business needed to digitize its commercial channel without losing the agility that wholesale customers expect when placing an order.
overview.p3: The goal wasn't just to have an online store — it was to build a tool that both salespeople and customers could use efficiently every day.

challenge.title: Challenge
challenge.c1desc: Orders scattered across calls and spreadsheets without standard guidelines.
challenge.c2desc: Items lacked clear categories, forcing buyers to require deep institutional store knowledge.
challenge.c3desc: No support for bulk volumes, tier pricing structures, or instant record retrieval.
challenge.c4desc: B2B buyers require efficient procurement tools; standard systems slowed down reordering scales.

beforeAfter.title: Before vs After
beforeAfter.desc: The order process went from manual and scattered to structured and self-managed.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.p1: The platform allows orders to be managed faster and more efficiently, reducing operational friction for both the internal team and customers.
outcome.p2: It establishes a solid foundation for digital channel growth without relying on manual processes.

bhb2b.title: Bulonera Hurlingham
bhb2b.intro: Design of a wholesale online store focused on efficient navigation and fast ordering for B2B buyers.

myRole.title: My Role
myRole.p1: I designed the wholesale purchasing experience, with particular attention to catalog structure and reducing friction in the order flow. The work included architecture decisions, visual hierarchy, and purchase process optimization.

overview.title: Context
overview.p1: Bulonera Hurlingham B2B is a wholesale hardware distributor with a customer base that places frequent, high-volume orders.
overview.p2: The challenge was building a platform that adapts to the wholesale buying rhythm: fast, direct, and with no unnecessary friction.
overview.p3: The experience had to work for customers who already know the catalog and know what they want — not for casual browsers.

challenge.title: Challenge
challenge.c1desc: The catalog wasn't organized for fast purchasing. Finding a product required too many steps.
challenge.c2desc: The purchase experience didn't reflect B2B buyer needs: quantities, technical references, reordering.
challenge.c3desc: Adding new products or categories was a costly and unsystematic process.

beforeAfter.title: Before vs After
beforeAfter.desc: Navigation went from slow and confusing to direct and purchase-oriented.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.p1: The new ecommerce reduces the time it takes a wholesale customer to find and order what they need.
outcome.p2: The catalog structure allows the business to scale without degrading the purchase experience.

bombas.title: Bombas y Servicios
bombas.intro: Corporate portal update to improve content organization and navigation experience.

myRole.title: My Role
myRole.p1: I designed the new site architecture and visual interface. The focus was on understanding how users access information and reorganizing content so that access is direct and frictionless.

overview.title: Context
overview.p1: The previous site had structural issues that made it difficult to access key business information.
overview.p2: In the industrial sector, credibility and clarity are directly tied to conversion. A confusing site translates into missed opportunities.

challenge.title: Challenge
challenge.c1desc: Content didn't follow a clear logic. Users had to actively search for what should have been immediately visible.
challenge.c2desc: The menu structure didn't reflect how users think. Orientation within the site required effort.
challenge.c3desc: The design didn't communicate the solidity and track record of the business. Brand perception was below reality.

beforeAfter.title: Before vs After
beforeAfter.desc: Key information went from scattered to hierarchical and accessible from the first moment.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.p1: The site allows users to access information directly, without friction, and with a visual presentation that reflects the solidity of the business.
outcome.p2: It becomes an active commercial credibility tool, not just a passive digital presence.

comafer.title: Comafer
comafer.intro: Ecommerce redesign focused on organizing an extensive catalog and improving the search and navigation experience.

myRole.title: My Role
myRole.p1: I designed the new site structure treating it as a system, not just a set of screens. The work included category reorganization, information hierarchy, and search flow optimization for a high-volume catalog.

overview.title: Context
overview.p1: Comafer manages an extensive catalog in the hardware sector, with multiple categories, subcategories, and product variants.
overview.p2: The core problem wasn't the number of products — it was the difficulty of finding them. A large, poorly organized catalog is worse than a small, well-structured one.
overview.p3: The challenge was building an architecture that scales with the business without degrading the purchase experience.

challenge.title: Challenge
challenge.c1desc: The legacy look failed to convey the premium nature and corporate reliability of Comafer's massive operations.
challenge.c2desc: Structuring large-scale corporate data and contact funnels into a balanced, clear layout.
challenge.c3desc: Establishing a rigid frontend design framework that preserves aesthetic appeal across all corporate viewports.
challenge.c4desc: Streamlining search indexing parameters to minimize catalog checkout drop-offs.

beforeAfter.title: Before vs After
beforeAfter.desc: Navigation went from confusing and deep to direct, clear, and decision-oriented.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.p1: The new site improves navigation speed and reduces friction in product search, making purchasing decisions easier for wholesale buyers.
outcome.p2: The architecture is prepared to grow with the catalog without degrading the experience.

fjg.title: FJG Impermeabilizaciones
fjg.intro: Design of a clear and direct landing page to communicate waterproofing services and facilitate contact with potential clients.

myRole.title: My Role
myRole.p1: I designed the landing from start to finish, making all decisions around structure, content hierarchy, and calls to action. The goal was clear: the user arrives, understands what FJG offers, and makes contact without friction.

overview.title: Context
overview.p1: FJG Impermeabilizaciones needed a digital presence that reflects professionalism and allows potential clients to get in touch simply and directly.
overview.p2: In services, trust is built before the first contact. The site had to convey credibility and make taking the next step easy.

challenge.title: Challenge
challenge.c1desc: There was no clear presentation of the services offered. Visitors didn't know what to do or what to expect.
challenge.c2desc: Services were described generically, without differentiating value proposition or use cases.
challenge.c3desc: Without a clear and accessible call to action, the digital channel generated very few real inquiries.

beforeAfter.title: Before vs After
beforeAfter.desc: The digital presence went from nonexistent to an active client acquisition tool.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.p1: The site improves the business presentation and facilitates contact, functioning as an active lead generation channel.
outcome.p2: Clear structure and visible calls to action reduce the friction between user interest and first contact.

netegia.title: Netegia
netegia.intro: Website restructuring to improve comprehension of a management system with multiple modules and functionalities.

myRole.title: My Role
myRole.p1: I worked on the site's content architecture, reorganizing product information so potential clients can understand what the system does, how it's organized, and why it's valuable — without needing a demo first.

overview.title: Context
overview.p1: Netegia is an ERP system with multiple modules covering different business areas: administration, inventory, invoicing, logistics.
overview.p2: The challenge of communicating a complex product is that internal complexity cannot be transferred to the visitor. The site has to do the simplification work that the software can't do on its own.
overview.p3: A potential client who doesn't understand the product in the first 30 seconds doesn't convert. Content architecture was the core problem.

challenge.title: Challenge
challenge.c1desc: An ERP has many features. Without a clear structure, presenting everything is equivalent to presenting nothing relevant.
challenge.c2desc: The previous site didn't distinguish between what users need to know first and what is implementation detail.
challenge.c3desc: It wasn't clear what problem Netegia solves or what type of business it's designed for.

beforeAfter.title: Before vs After
beforeAfter.desc: The value proposition went from buried among features to visible from the first moment.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.p1: The site improves product comprehension and makes it easier for potential clients to understand its value without needing an external explanation.
outcome.p2: The module-based organization allows progressive exploration of the system without overwhelming users with technical information from the start.

zafirofarm.title: Zafiro Farmacias
zafirofarm.intro: Update of a pharmacy's ERP website to achieve a clearer, more modern and usable experience aligned with the business level.

myRole.title: My Role
myRole.p1: I designed the new site experience, improving navigation structure, visual hierarchy, and brand presentation. The work was oriented toward aligning digital perception with the real level of the business.

overview.title: Context
overview.p1: The previous site didn't reflect the level or track record of the business. The navigation experience was confusing and the design communicated an outdated image.
overview.p2: In health retail, trust and clarity are critical values. A site that doesn't convey them operates at a disadvantage against competitors with better digital presence.

challenge.title: Challenge
challenge.c1desc: The site's aesthetic didn't match the quality and seriousness of the business. The first impression created a negative gap.
challenge.c2desc: Users had difficulty finding basic information: locations, services, contact.
challenge.c3desc: Most traffic comes from mobile. The site wasn't adapted for that experience.

beforeAfter.title: Before vs After
beforeAfter.desc: Brand perception went from outdated to coherent with the real quality of the business.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.p1: The site improves brand perception and user experience, aligning with the real level of the business.
outcome.p2: Clear navigation and responsive design allow any user, on any device, to access what they need without friction.

otraronda.title: Otra Ronda
otraronda.intro: Full digital presence redesign to transform a bar service into a professional, attractive, and conversion-oriented brand.

myRole.title: My Role
myRole.p1: I handled the brand and site redesign, from the page structure to the contact form.

overview.title: Context
overview.p1: OtraRonda is a bar service for events that was in an early growth stage.
overview.p2: They already had an online presence, but it failed to convey the level of experience and quality their service actually delivered. The gap between business reality and digital image was the core problem.
overview.p3: The challenge was to build a digital identity that matches their evolution and allows them to compete in a highly visual and aspirational market.

challenge.title: Challenge
challenge.c1desc: The generic interface undermined user trust, creating an artificial gap between the online image and the high-end physical execution.
challenge.c2desc: The dynamic nature of social media channels showcasing real event atmosphere was completely isolated from the web.
challenge.c3desc: A rigid, outdated form system prevented prospective clients from navigating menus or exploring specific service formats easily.
challenge.c4desc: The structural architecture lacked explicit calls-to-action, dropping hot commercial user interest before acquisition.

beforeAfter.title: Before vs After
beforeAfter.desc: The digital identity went from generic and misaligned to a brand with character, visual coherence, and commercial direction.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.p1: The new site positions OtraRonda as a more professional, trustworthy, and attractive offering within its market.
outcome.p2: The experience better communicates the service value and facilitates contact, becoming a real client acquisition tool.

notes.title: Reflection
notes.p1: This project reflects how clear structure and a well-defined aesthetic can transform the perception of a venture and accelerate its growth. Visual identity is not decoration — it's positioning.
